overview: The City Council received an update on the municipal electricity aggregation program, requested a safety briefing regarding the 911 dispatch system, and addressed concerns about sex offender housing at a local nursing facility.

items.title: Municipal Aggregation Program Update
items.summary: Alicia Hunt and consultants reported that the community energy program added 3.6 million kilowatt-hours of renewable energy to the grid, though participants paid an average of $4 more than basic service over the first 10 months. The Council approved motions for quarterly program updates and for the city to provide residents with clearer market rate comparison data.

items.title: 911 Dispatch System Concerns
items.summary: Councilors questioned a communication from the Mayor describing a 911 supervisor vacancy as an emergency and requested that the Police and Fire Chiefs, Lieutenant Rudolph, and the dispatchers' union representative attend a future meeting to clarify public safety status. Members expressed concern over a lack of unified training manuals and protocol after 18 months of civilian dispatch operations.

items.title: Resolutions and License Items
items.summary: The Council congratulated Congresswoman Catherine Clark on her election as Assistant Speaker of the House and requested that police notify an out-of-town trucking company to find suitable parking for tractor-trailers currently using Commercial Street.

items.title: Housing of Level 3 Sex Offenders
items.summary: The Council requested policy information from a local rehabilitation center and a summary of city notification procedures following reports that multiple high-level sex offenders were residing at a residential nursing facility. An amendment was approved to include links to the sex offender registry on city and school websites to improve public transparency.

items.title: Social Justice Roadmap Update
items.summary: Councilor Morell requested progress reports on the SNAP gap study, police policy reviews, and community conversations on racism; the Chief of Staff noted that a coordinator is being hired to assist residents with qualifying for food resources. A companion motion was approved requiring the administration to provide all future program updates to the Council in writing.

items.title: Main and South Street Intersection Safety
items.summary: The Transportation Subcommittee reported on a meeting with MassDOT regarding the intersection, which is ranked among the most dangerous in the state, noting that a permanent light system is three to five years away. The Council is pursuing immediate low-cost traffic calming measures while the state evaluates signalization for the entire corridor.

items.title: Zoning Ordinance Review
items.summary: The Committee of the Whole met with a consultant to review the city's zoning use tables and compare them to similarly sized municipalities.
